title: Reservation governor rationalization and noisy-tenant surge remediation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: During the 2025-02-10 capacity incident a single tenant's sudden high-concurrency, long-sequence workload exhausted pooled reservations and triggered widespread soft-evictions and tail latency spikes across two dedicated GPU pools. Root cause is a combination of: (1) reservation sizing that counts only active workers and ignores transient KV cache and per-request memory, (2) an aggressive instantaneous burst allowance that can deplete shared credits, and (3) the admission controller's eviction-first behavior under burst pressure which amplifies noisy neighbor effects. Impact: several customers experienced >10x tail latency and a small number of requests were retried/failed; production SLA targets were breached for ~45 minutes. Goals for this ticket: remediate immediate regressions, add deterministic safety nets so a single tenant cannot cause cross-tenant tail latency, and create reproducible test coverage to prevent regressions in allocator/burst logic.
comments: 2025-02-12 — Aisha Kapoor: Initial postmortem notes posted to Confluence + triggered dedicated-capacity stability project. Triage determined this is P0 because of SLA impact. Assigned to Miguel for remediation plan.

2025-02-13 — Miguel Santos: Performed heap/profile and telemetry sweep. Observed KV cache allocations and per-request scratch memory were effectively invisible to reservation accounting. Drafted three-signal tenant score: (cpu_seconds, kv_mem_bytes, qps_weighted) to drive admission decisions.

2025-02-15 — Claire Huang (SRE): Ran synthetic repro in staging using the new synthetic-load harness. Reproducer shows eviction storm at 80% pooled reservation consumption. Confirmed admission controller is choosing eviction over rejecting low-priority bursts.

2025-02-17 — Product (Jon Park): Agreed on conservative rollout: introduce soft caps + signal-based tenant throttling for initial rollout; do not change billing semantics. Product wants an observability dashboard showing per-tenant reservation burn and burst budget over time.
2025-02-18 — Miguel Santos: Opened prototype PR that implements per-tenant KV cache cap and an amortized 10-minute burst budget window. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/14582
2025-02-20 — Aisha Kapoor: Review feedback from runtime team added: need graceful degradation path that prefers model-variant fallback before evicting other tenants. Add to action items.
action_items: Implement tenant fingerprinting: enrich tenant descriptor with sequence-length histogram and kv-cache footprint (owner: Miguel, estimate: 3)
Add per-tenant KV cache soft-cap with telemetry and alerting (owner: runtime-team/Sana, estimate: 2)
Replace 'evict-first' admission policy with 'reject-low-priority-burst' policy + traffic-class admission controller (owner: Miguel, estimate: 2)
Introduce an amortized burst budget (rolling 10-minute window) with explicit budget meters and grace tokens; surface in Console (owner: infra/Elena, estimate: 3)
Add conservative hysteresis to reservation autoscaler to reduce flapping (owner: autoscale-team, estimate: 2)
Create a staging synthetic-load suite to run on PRs touching allocator/burst policy; include eviction and latency assertions (owner: SRE, estimate: 4)
Dashboard and alerting: per-tenant reservation burn, burst budget remaining, eviction rate, and 99/99.9 latencies for affected pools (owner: Observability, estimate: 2)
Run a canary rollout (5% of pools) for the new admission controller and KV cap before cluster-wide activation (owner: Miguel, estimate: 1)
Document changes and update runbooks with playbook for noisy neighbor detection and soft-quarantine steps (owner: SRE, estimate: 1)
Post-deploy retrospective: validate unit economics impact and rollout telemetry for 72 hours; rollback plan if false-positive rejections exceed threshold (owner: Product + Runtime, estimate: 1)
links: Prototype PR for KV cap and burst amortization: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/14582
runbook_updates: Add a 'noisy-tenant' section that includes: detection thresholds (eviction_rate > 0.5% and 99.9 latency increase > 2x over baseline), immediate soft-quarantine steps (set tenant admission to limited-burst, cap KV cache to 25% of tenant's historical peak, enable model-variant fallback), and escalation path. Include commands for forcing per-pool admission controller to 'reject' mode and safe rollback steps. Link runbook to incident dashboard and make runbook editable by SRE on-call.
